name: Ritual
oneLine: A ritual isn't empty small talk - it's a fixed-price stroke exchange, and people keep close count of exactly what's owed.
whatYouDid: You built Mr. C's welcome-back greeting after two weeks away - too thin ("hey", keep walking) and he felt snubbed, too much and it read like a sales pitch, matched and it landed exactly as a greeting should.
confusion: People treat rituals as meaningless filler; the tell is how sharply it's felt when a ritual stroke gets shorted - imagine offering a handshake and having it ignored.

fromBook.quote: The participants in a ritual will often keep a close count of the strokes exchanged.

expand.definition: Rituals are stereotyped social exchanges, programmed in Parent and carried out in (usually positive) Adapted Child, whose whole value is predictability - a simple one like "Hi / Hi" costs one stroke each way, an elaborate one (a homecoming, a religious service) costs far more, but the exchange is always precisely accounted for.
expand.otherFraming: TA Today notes rituals are perceived from Child as riskier than withdrawal, but their predictability is exactly what makes them useful for topping up the stroke bank safely.
expand.tryThisToday: Notice the next ritual greeting you give or get, and whether it actually matches what the moment calls for - too little, and watch for the other person's flicker of offense.
